reviewer: Codex primary final critical reading; selected separate-reader findings retained in evidence/reviews. No human/Claude acceptance claimed.

clarity.evidence: Two customers competing for two show seats introduces hold ownership before payment vocabulary.

scope.evidence: Finished all-seat reservation/payment design; one monitor is the executable boundary and row transactions are a separately described extension.

contracts.evidence: Show-seat keys, immutable quote, reservation owner and separate refund/reconciliation facts agree across prose and code.

correctness.evidence: BookingChecks passes 111 checks with 40 rounds of 40 contenders; insert-on-conflict request creation precedes row locking in the database protocol.

failure_handling.evidence: Deadline equality expires the hold; late first-consistent capture creates a refund intent without releasing a new owner; contradictory receipts are quarantined.

tradeoffs.evidence: Firm expiry versus grace, monitor versus database locks, and durable payment reconciliation are defended with answered follow-ups.

visual_learning.evidence: booking.json is emitted by BookingTrace: both race winners and late-capture ownership are stepped explicitly.

code.evidence: examples/learning-java/src/kb/booking; full copyable source/download parity and exact excerpts checked by check_review_lot.py; actual runtime output in lot-command-output.json and lot-runtime.json.

rendering.evidence: LLD-4-browser.json: article and walkthrough in light/dark at 1280/390px; theme controls, navigation, no missing images/page-wide overflow, table contrast >=4.5. Per-topic assets resolve.

limits: Local mechanism and fixture checks do not establish remote-provider behavior, distributed durability/failover, production throughput or model quality. Scope-specific boundaries are explicit in the answer.
